chunks: And ʿAlī عليه السلام was asked: “Is it more beloved to you that wudu (ablution) be performed from the leftover water of a group of Muslims, or that wudu (ablution) be performed from a covered white vessel?” So he said:
“No; rather, from the leftover water of the group of Muslims, for indeed the most beloved of your religion to Allah is the upright, tolerant, easy path.”

key_terms.الْحَنِيفِيَّةُ: the upright religion inclined away from falsehood toward truth
key_terms.وُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before worship

ai.seo_question: Is it preferable to perform wudu (ablution) from the leftover water of other Muslims or from separate stored water?
ai.summary: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام prefers using the leftover water from the wudu (ablution) of a group of Muslims over water kept separately in a covered vessel. The hadith indicates ease, openness, and communal simplicity within the religion, presenting the dīn beloved to Allah as upright, tolerant, and easy.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.16 - Ameerul Momineen Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) was asked: "Is it better to perform ablution from the leftover water of a group of Muslims, or from a covered white jug?"
Imam (as) said: "No, rather from the leftover water of the group of Muslims, for the most beloved aspect of your religion to Allah (swt) is the tolerant and agreeable monotheism."
